audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: Quote check passes on all three legs at the stated pages. The classification (non-phonemic stress on the root-initial syllable, prefixes outside the domain; long vowels attract stress per Temple) rests on a 2021 reference grammar of a sister language making a blanket family-wide claim, plus two colonial comparative works (1898, 1903) whose statements are group-wide and Bea-based; nothing is Kol-specific, and nothing Kol-specific will ever be written since the language died with a handful of speakers c. 1900-1920 (Portman already had only three informants). Glottolog confirms no grammar/phonology/sketch exists for akak1253. So the record holds essentially the best available statements and nothing seen suggests the classification is wrong -- 'thin' rather than 'at-risk'. The one refinement found: Portman's Kol vocabulary column carries stress underlines (lost in our scanned, visible in the archive.org

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.quote: Portman marks stress by underlining a syllable; unmarked words are stressed on the first syllable (p. 29). The acute/macron diacritics are vowel quality/length per the alphabet key (pp. 28-29), not stress. In the scans the underlines survive: vocab p. 27 Kol 'Karábat-che' (centipede) has the second-syllable a underlined, i.e. a Kol word with marked non-initial stress; neighbouring Juwoi forms 'Rá-chelúkāū', '-lekíle' are likewise underlined. Most Kol entries on the page are unmarked (default initial).
sources.locator: Comparative Vocabulary p. 27, Kol column (with main-text p. 29 convention and alphabet pp. 28-29)
sources.note: The only Kol-specific stress evidence in existence is Portman's syllable underlines in the Kol column; our held scanned strips them. Sample downloaded now shows at least one Kol root with marked second-syllable stress (Karábat 'centipede'), so a pass over the Kol column would turn 'exceptions: none-stated' into an actual count and test the root-initial default on Kol data rather than on a family-wide sentence.
